title: replaced the casualOS map with leaflet
summary: Maps of Bible places, from the **Locations** verse button and from **Theographic Data** place cards, are now drawn on a lightweight OpenStreetMap street map instead of the slow embedded CasualOS map. They should open in about a second instead of 5–10, land the place in the right spot, show who the map and place data come from, dim in dark mode, and offer a **Back to the place** button.

links.label: Issue 2054: Faster, lighter maps: replace the CasualOS map view with Leaflet

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the button above, in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If it looks like the old version, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac).

setup.title: Start clean and sign in
setup.body: Use a private/incognito window, so nothing is left over from earlier visits. Sign in with your email address (you'll be sent a code, so use an inbox you can check). Installing extensions needs an account.

setup.title: Install Locations and Theographic Data
setup.body: Open **Settings**, then **Extensions**. Under **Available**, install **Locations** and **Theographic Data**. If either is already under **Installed**, leave it. If you can't find one of them, mark the tests that use it **Blocked** and say so in the note.

setup.title: Use a light theme to start
setup.body: The first tests assume the app's light theme. One later test switches to dark mode.

sections.title: Maps from the Locations verse button
sections.intro: Click a verse that names a place, then use the **Locations** button in the verse toolbar.

tests.title: A place opens on a street map within about a second
tests.why: The main point of the change: the old map took 5–10 seconds because it started a whole CasualOS app. The very first map may take a moment longer while the map code downloads once.
steps: Open **John 2** and click verse **John 2:1** (it mentions Cana) so the verse toolbar appears.
Click the **Locations** button in the toolbar, then choose **Show Cana on map**.
Watch the floating panel that opens and note roughly how long it takes until the map appears.
expected: A floating panel titled **Cana** opens. A grey placeholder may show briefly, then a street map with roads and town names appears, usually within a second or two.
A filled dot marks Cana, with a small **Cana** label above it.
Cana is in northern Israel, inland between the Mediterranean coast and the Sea of Galilee, a little north of Nazareth. It is **not** on the island of Cyprus or out at sea.

tests.title: A second map opens instantly
tests.why: Once the map code has downloaded, later maps shouldn't wait for it again.
tests.before: You opened the Cana map in the previous test.
steps: Close the Cana panel.
Still on **John 2**, click **John 2:12** (it mentions Capernaum), then **Locations** › **Show Capernaum on map**.
expected: The Capernaum map appears almost at once, with no long wait.
Capernaum sits right on the northern shore of the Sea of Galilee (the lake), not inland and not in the sea.

tests.title: Places from the hand-built place list land in the right spot
tests.why: About 800 places come from a hand-built list that stores coordinates in reverse order. The app now flips them as they load; if that's wrong, these places land hundreds of miles away (around Cyprus or Turkey).
steps: Open **Acts 21** and click **Acts 21:7** (it mentions Ptolemais).
Click **Locations** › **Show Ptolemais on map**.
expected: Ptolemais (also known as Acco or Akko) is on the Mediterranean coast in northern Israel, just north of the city of Haifa across the bay.
The bottom corner of the map shows a credit with **© OpenStreetMap**. There is no **OpenBible.info** credit for this place, because it isn't OpenBible's data.

tests.title: OpenBible places land in the right spot and credit OpenBible
tests.why: The other place list (from OpenBible.info) is already in the standard order and should not be flipped. Its license requires a credit on the map.
steps: Open **John 2** again and click **John 2:1** (it also mentions Galilee).
Click **Locations** › **Show Galilee on map**.
expected: The map shows the Galilee region in northern Israel, around the Sea of Galilee, with the whole shape in view (outlined or marked, depending on the data).
The credit in the bottom corner shows both **© OpenStreetMap** and **Places: OpenBible.info (CC BY 4.0)**. Both links open their websites.

tests.title: A large place (an island outline) draws and fits in the panel
tests.why: Big outlines such as Crete couldn't be shown by the old map at all. Now the whole outline should be drawn and the map zoomed out enough to show it.
steps: Open **Acts 27** and click **Acts 27:7** (it mentions Crete).
Click **Locations** › **Show Crete on map**.
expected: The panel shows the island of Crete in the Mediterranean, south of Greece, with the whole island in view.
The page stays responsive; it does not freeze.

tests.title: Zooming, panning and the Back to the place button
tests.why: New on this map: a button that returns the view to the place after you've moved around.
steps: Open any place map from the Locations button (for example **Show Cana on map** on **John 2:1**).
Use the **+** and **−** buttons in the map's top-left corner to zoom in and out. Scroll the mouse wheel over the map. Drag the map somewhere far away.
Click the round target button in the map's top-right corner. Hover over it first to see its name.
expected: Zooming and dragging move the map smoothly, and new map pieces fill in as you move.
The button's name is **Back to the place**. Clicking it returns the map to the place, as it was first shown.

tests.title: Resizing or moving the floating panel keeps the map filled
steps: Open a place map from the Locations button.
Drag the panel to another spot, then drag its edge or corner to make it much bigger, then much smaller.
expected: The map always fills the panel. There are no grey or empty strips after resizing.
The map doesn't reload or flash back to a placeholder while you drag or resize.

tests.title: Opening the same place twice doesn't stack two panels
steps: Open **Show Cana on map** from **John 2:1** and leave the panel open.
Click **John 2:1** again and choose **Locations** › **Show Cana on map** again.
expected: There is still only one **Cana** map panel, not two on top of each other.

sections.title: Maps in Theographic Data place cards
sections.intro: Theographic Data shows place cards in the Discover content at the bottom of a chapter. An expanded place card has a small map in it.

tests.title: A place card shows a small map, and the page scrolls past it
tests.why: The card's map sits inside scrolling content, so the mouse wheel should scroll the page, not zoom the map.
steps: Open **John 2** and scroll to the Discover content at the bottom of the chapter.
Open the **Places** section and click the card for **Cana** so it expands.
With the mouse pointer over the small map, scroll the mouse wheel up and down.
expected: The expanded card shows a small street map with Cana marked and labelled, in the same spot as in the Locations test.
Scrolling the wheel over the map scrolls the page; the map does not zoom.
The map's top-right corner has the **Open in map** button and the **Back to the place** button.

tests.title: Open in map opens the place in its own panel
tests.before: The Cana card is expanded (previous test).
steps: Click the **Open in map** button in the small map's top-right corner (hover to see its name).
Look at the card again, then close the floating panel.
expected: A floating panel titled **Cana** opens with the map.
While the panel is open, the card hides its own small map. After you close the panel, the small map comes back in the card.

tests.title: A place with no map file still lands in the right spot
tests.why: When a place isn't in Locations' lists, Theographic Data draws a point from its own coordinates. That point's coordinate order was changed in this PR; if wrong, the place lands far away.
steps: Open **Genesis 12** and scroll to the Discover content at the bottom.
Open **Places** and expand the card for **Egypt** (or **Haran**, if Egypt isn't listed).
Look at where the marker is on the small map.
expected: Egypt's marker is in Egypt, in north-east Africa (Haran's is in south-east Turkey, near the Syrian border).
It is not in the Mediterranean Sea, Libya, or the Arabian Peninsula.

tests.title: Crete opens from a place card
tests.why: Before this change, Theographic Data had to fall back to a single dot for big places like Crete. Now it should draw the island.
steps: Open **Acts 27**, scroll to the Discover content, open **Places** and expand the card for **Crete** (if it's listed).
Click **Open in map**.
expected: The small map and the panel both show the island of Crete, south of Greece, with the whole island in view.
The credit in the corner includes **Places: OpenBible.info (CC BY 4.0)**.

sections.title: Dark mode, phones and connection problems

tests.title: Maps dim to match dark mode
steps: Switch the app to its dark theme in **Settings**.
Open **Show Cana on map** from **John 2:1**, and expand the **Cana** place card at the bottom of **John 2**.
Switch back to the light theme while the map is open.
expected: In dark mode, the street map is dark (dark background, light roads and text), not a bright white map. Labels and the place marker are still easy to read.
The zoom buttons, credit and **Back to the place** button match the dark theme.
Switching back to light shows the normal bright map again.

tests.title: Maps work on a phone
tests.why: On a phone, swiping over the small card map should scroll the page, and the **Open in map** button is not offered.
steps: Open the preview link on a phone (or make a computer browser window as narrow as it goes and reload).
Open **John 2**, tap **John 2:1**, tap **Locations** › **Show Cana on map**. Pinch to zoom and drag the map.
Close the map. Scroll to the Discover content, expand the **Cana** place card, and swipe up and down with your finger starting on the small map.
expected: The map opens full screen, fills it, and zooms and pans with your fingers.
On the card, swiping over the small map scrolls the page instead of getting stuck moving the map.
The card's map has no **Open in map** button on a phone.

tests.title: No connection gives a clear message, not a blank panel
tests.why: Maps load their data from the internet. When that fails, the panel should say so. Exactly which message appears depends on what failed to download.
tests.before: Open a fresh private window, sign in, and open **John 2**, but don't open any map yet.
steps: Turn off Wi-Fi (or turn on airplane mode).
Click **John 2:1**, then **Locations** › **Show Cana on map**.
If you see a **Try again** button, turn Wi-Fi back on and click it. Otherwise turn Wi-Fi back on, close the panel and open the map again.
expected: While offline, the panel shows **This place can't be shown on the map.** or **The map couldn't load.** with a **Try again** button. It is not left blank or stuck on a grey placeholder forever.
Once back online, the map appears.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: A verse with no places has no Locations button
steps: Click a verse that names no place, for example **John 3:16**.
expected: The verse toolbar appears without a **Locations** button.

tests.title: The map stays under menus and other panels
tests.why: The map library draws its own buttons on high layers; the change keeps them inside the map so they don't cover the rest of the app.
steps: Open a place map from the Locations button and leave it open.
Open the app's main menu, a verse's toolbar menu, and **Settings**, so each appears over or next to the map panel.
expected: Menus, dropdowns and the Settings screen appear on top of the map. The map's **+**/**−** buttons and credit never show through on top of them.

notCovered: That the map code isn't downloaded when the app first starts, and that the startup download didn't grow. That needs the browser's developer tools or a build size report, so it's left to the code review.
Whether the libraries and data are licensed in a way the project can use; that's a review of the code and the credits, not something to click through.
The automated tests added for the coordinate flip, the map component and the map loader.
